messages:
From: Mike Allen <mike.allen@finsecure.com>

Cc: procurements@finsecure.com
Date: 2025-07-19T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Incident reporting, alerting & escalation — FinSecure

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — we're gathering detailed responses for our procurement and security teams as part of FinSecure's vendor RFI. A few specific asks we need answered in writing:

1) Incident detection & reporting: what automated signals do you emit for misuse or model misuse? How quickly are incidents categorized and surfaced to customers?
2) Alerting & thresholds: can we configure alert thresholds per account and receive paging with on-call details?
3) Escalation & SLAs: what are response/acknowledgement SLAs for critical security incidents? Do you provide a post-incident root cause summary?
4) Evidence & retention: retention windows for audit logs, content KV caches, and whether Redwood can produce logs for audits (format and timelines).
5) Access to forensic artifacts: can you provide request-level data or do you redact user-provided content?

We're aiming to complete vendor scoring by end of next week. If you can return a written response and any sample runbooks / SLA templates that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Allen
Head of Platform Security, FinSecure
(mike.allen@finsecure.com)

(Attachment: vendor-questionnaire-v2.xlsx (XLSX, 14KB))

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFI: Incident reporting, alerting & escalation — FinSecure

Hi Mike — appreciate the clear list. Below are concise answers plus attached artifacts; happy to expand any section in a short call. I've cc'd Laura (security) and Neha (product) for any legal/SLA details.

1) Incident detection & reporting
- Signals: automated misuse detectors (policy-guided classifiers), anomaly detectors on request rate/prompt patterns, model-output safety filters, and customer-provided prompt-sets for regression detection.
- Categorization: we tag incidents by severity (P0–P3) using a deterministic ruleset and ML-backed scoring; initial automated categorization occurs within 1–5 minutes of detection.
- Customer notifications: customers receive an initial alert (email + webhook) for P0/P1 within our acknowledgement SLA (see SLAs below).

2) Alerting & thresholds
- Tenant-configurable alerting: customers can set thresholds for rate anomalies, high-policy-violation ratios, or custom signal hooks via the Console or API.
- Notification channels: email, webhook, pagerduty (or custom integration). Onboarding includes a default on-call rotation config; customers can supply their PagerDuty service key.

3) Escalation & SLAs
- Acknowledgement SLA: P0 incidents acknowledged within 30 minutes; P1 within 2 hours (during business hours for non-enterprise support tiers; enterprise contracts can expand to 24/7 coverage).
- Remediation timeline: depends on incident type; immediate mitigation (model fallback & routing) is often applied in minutes while root-cause investigation proceeds.
- Post-incident package: searchable incident timeline, RCA draft, customer impact summary, and mitigation artifacts delivered within 10 business days for P0/P1 incidents.

4) Evidence & retention
- Audit logs: request-level metadata (timestamps, model variant, token counts, request ids) retained by default for 90 days; optional enterprise retention tiers available up to 7 years.
- KV cache & truncated artifacts: ephemeral content caches used for performance are rotated hourly and not retained long-term by default. For forensic requests, we preserve request traces and server-side metadata; we do not provide full unredacted user-submitted content unless requested under contract and with appropriate legal controls.
- Export formats: logs provided as gzipped JSON or CSV. Typical delivery time for ad-hoc forensic exports: 3–7 business days.

5) Forensic artifacts & access controls
- Role-based access: exports require authorized contacts and audit sign-off; we support signed data requests via our Console and SSO-based approval workflows.
- Redaction policy: by default, PII and user-provided content is masked in exports unless a contract amendment specifies otherwise.

Attachments included with this response:
- incident_reporting_and_escalation_rfi_answers.docx (detailed Q&A, 6 pages)
- runbook-sample.pdf (example mitigation runbook)

Next steps: If useful, propose a 30-minute call to walk the runbook and tailor SLA wording for FinSecure's procurement. Availability: Wed/Thu next week morning PT.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Mike — thanks, and great questions. Final clarifications below; attaching an SLA PDF and our detailed RFI doc with Laura's addendum. Also included is a suggested procurement line-item for expedited exports.

- False positives: baseline FP for P0/P1 automated flags is <0.5% across mixed production traffic (we track precision/recall internally and surface trends via the Console). Customers can tune sensitivity or add their own post-filter hooks.
- Payload persistence: by default, full request payloads are not persisted in plaintext logs. We record request ids, model variant, token counts, timestamps, and a cryptographic hash of prompt content for deduping/forensics. If a customer requires full payload retention for compliance, that is available by contract with strict access controls (RBAC + signed export requests).
- Expedited exports: enterprise customers may request a 48–72 hour expedited export for critical compliance investigations; cost and notice terms are outlined in the SLA.

Attached: support-sla-offer.pdf (SLA + expedited export T&Cs), incident_reporting_and_escalation_rfi_answers.docx (updated with FP baseline and retention notes), runbook-sample.pdf

Best regards,
